chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad from Hariz from one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the moon is eclipsed, if a man wakes up and is sluggish to pray, he should perform a ritual bath (ghusl) tomorrow and make up the prayer; and if he did not wake up and did not know of the moon's eclipse, then upon him is only making up the prayer without a bath."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up lunar eclipse prayer if one slept through it?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* distinguishes between negligence and genuine oversight in performing the lunar eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf). It establishes that ritual bath (ghusl) is a specific penalty for laziness after waking, whereas simple forgetfulness or unawareness requires only the makeup prayer (qada), reflecting the Shia principle of ease in cases of unintentional omission.
